title: Aerolith POC: SSO, Audit Logs & Data Retention - Weekly Sync
summary: Weekly checkpoint on POC security gates: SSO integration status, audit log format/retention, SOC 2 evidence ask, and a quick review of host vs dedicated routing for sensitive traffic. Action items landed on sharing SOC2 pack and a small audit-log sample export for Dan to validate ingestion pipeline.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for sensitive tokens
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 package + compliance slide deck (Maya) by 2025-08-01
Customer to validate audit log sample against SIEM (Daniel) by 2025-08-05
Schedule in-prod sign-off meeting after log validation (Priya to propose times)
Luis to provide short how-to for mapping Redwood audit fields to Aerolith SIEM
action_items: Maya Chen: Share SOC2 report and minimal compliance pack (2025-08-01)
Luis Ortega: Export 24h audit log sample and redact PII, upload to shared link (2025-07-31)
Daniel Park: Run sample through SIEM and report mismatches (2025-08-05)
Riya Mehta: Confirm retention window requirements and legal holds (2025-08-04)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Aerolith Head of Infra), Riya Mehta (Aerolith Security Lead), Omar El-Sayed (Aerolith Platform)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check—can folks hear me okay?
[00:04] Daniel Park: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:06] Riya Mehta: same here.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Great. This is our weekly POC sync - want to focus today on the SSO status, audit log format, data retention policy, and the SOC2 artefacts you asked for. Luis will walk through the log payload and mapping briefly.
[00:22] Luis Ortega: Hi all. Quick note, I posted the short log schema in the shared drive—link in the calendar invite. I'm going to screen-share the example pulse, uh, sample payload. Apologies, our recorder sometimes tags it as "log pail" in the export.
[00:35] Omar El-Sayed: I couldn't find the link in the invite — is it separate?
[00:38] Priya Nair: I can re-share after; will drop in the chat.
[00:41] Luis Ortega: cool thanks.
[00:45] [01:05] Luis Ortega: (screen) So the audit log has three main sections: request metadata (timestamp, route, model_version), identity context (user_id, session_id, auth_method), and content metadata (tokens_sent, tokens_generated, truncated_flag). We also include an action field when something like model fallback or routing occurs.
[01:25] Riya Mehta: When you say identity context — is user_id PII? We need to know what you consider PII for our legal team.
[01:32] Luis Ortega: Good q. user_id is a hashed ID by default; we can also ship a fully anonymized id if you prefer. The sample we put in the drive is already redacted.
[01:41] Daniel Park: What file format — JSONL, right? And how's delivery—S3 push or webhook?
[01:46] Luis Ortega: It's JSONL. Delivery options: S3 push to a customer bucket, or we can stream to an HTTPS endpoint with HMAC auth. For aerolith, you said SIEM pulls from S3?
[01:54] Daniel Park: Yes, SIEM pulls every 5 minutes. Ideally we want a put to our S3 with server-side encryption and object lock for legal hold.
[02:02] Maya Chen: We can do S3 delivery with SSE-KMS and support object lock settings. We'll need the S3 ARN and bucket policy we should publish to enable a put role.
[02:12] Riya Mehta: Also need retention controls — we can't keep logs more than 2 years, and some classes must be 6 months only.
[02:20] Maya Chen: Understood. Our retention parameter on the delivery side can be set per customer; we can also optionally strip payloads older than X days on Redwood side before pushing to you — but if you require audit trails we recommend we keep a master copy for 90 days for troubleshooting then push final copy to your S3 where you control retention.
[02:36] Daniel Park: We prefer single-source in our S3 for auditing. If Redwood keeps a copy for troubleshooting, it should be made explicit in SLA.
[02:44] Priya Nair: We can add that to the POC addendum: explicit retention/temporary debug copy policy and deletion windows.
[02:50] [03:15] Riya Mehta: On SSO—Dan raised earlier that Aerolith uses Okta and we've started the SAML metadata exchange. What's outstanding?
[03:23] Maya Chen: From Redwood side, initial SAML config was completed last week. Luis, can you remind folks of the Assertion attributes we expect?
[03:29] Luis Ortega: Sure—email, groups, and a transient nameID. We also accept an attribute called azure_ad_upn if customers come from AAD. For Okta, we map groups to RBAC roles in Redwood.
[03:40] Omar El-Sayed: We're using group claims heavily. How granular can the mapping be—can we map multiple Okta groups to a single Redwood role?
[03:47] Luis Ortega: Yes you can map multiple groups to one role. Also note group sync happens at login, we cache for 15 minutes by default, can change if you need real-time enforcement.
[03:56] Riya Mehta: Cache means if someone is removed from a group, they might keep access for a bit — is there a way to force re-sync on our side?
[04:02] Luis Ortega: We have an admin API you can call to invalidate the cache per session or per user. We'll share that snippet.
[04:09] Maya Chen: Action: Luis share admin API snippet. (note made)
[04:12] [04:40] Daniel Park: SOC2 — you mentioned you have a report. We need evidence artifacts for control 6.2 and 7.1 for our procurement checklist. What's the quickest way for us to get those?
[04:50] Maya Chen: We have a SOC2 Type II report and a compliance pack. I can send the redacted report and a mapping doc that ties controls to evidence artifacts. We'll add a short cover letter that points to where to find logs and config screenshots.
[05:00] Riya Mehta: Redacted is fine. Legal will still request any subservice org letters?
[05:04] Maya Chen: We can provide subservice org info and the list of subprocessors. We'll also include our incident response playbook excerpt.
[05:11] [05:30] Omar El-Sayed: A small nit — in our SOC mapping we need the exact log field names so our SIEM queries can be written. The sample we saw uses "tokens_generated" but our SIEM expects "gen_tokens" — can mapping be configurable?
[05:40] Luis Ortega: Yes, mapping is configurable. We can provide a transform layer or a simple field alias config you supply. We'll push a sample transform the next day.
[05:47] Daniel Park: Great. Also curious about encryption keys—if we push to our S3 with SSE-KMS, who manages the key?
[05:54] Maya Chen: For S3 SSE-KMS, you can provide the KMS key in your account and we will encrypt with that. Redwood doesn't hold the key. For data at rest in Redwood's systems, we use our KMS with envelope encryption and can provide key rotation docs.
[06:08] Riya Mehta: Are there any retained caches in Redwood that contain unencrypted user content during inference?
[06:14] Luis Ortega: By default the KV cache is in memory on the inference nodes and not persisted; we do have option to persist for warm start which we disable for POCs with sensitive data. Any persisted caches would be encrypted at rest.
[06:27] [06:45] Riya Mehta: Audit logs — can we get an event for model fallback and for routing decisions? We need to be able to attribute a decision for forensic cases.
[06:53] Luis Ortega: Yes the event "routing_decision" is included and we emit a "fallback_reason" string. We also include pre/post model_version fields so you can see the before/after.
[07:03] Priya Nair: Quick note — earlier you asked about dedicated vs hosted for sensitive traffic. Where are you leaning?
[07:10] Daniel Park: For this POC we wanted to test the hosted path but with strong log shipping to our S3 and an agreement that sensitive payloads are not persisted beyond X hours. Long term, if vendor lock-in or compliance requires, we'll likely go dedicated.
[07:22] Maya Chen: That's a common pattern—test hosted then shift to dedicated for production. Our dedicated offering gives you isolated GPU pools and dedicated network egress. We'll detail the differences in the follow-up doc.
[07:33] [08:00] Omar El-Sayed: One integration snag we saw: during heavy load our session cache sometimes returns stale nameID which caused a login loop in staging. Is that a known issue?
[08:10] Luis Ortega: We had a bug in the cache invalidation which we patched last week. If you still see it, let us know session id and timestamp and we can trace.
[08:18] Daniel Park: We'll capture a repro if it reoccurs.
[08:22] [08:45] Riya Mehta: What's the proposed retention enforcement flow? If a legal hold is applied do you respect our bucket-level object lock?
[08:53] Maya Chen: If you use object lock on your bucket we will not overwrite or delete those objects from your side. For Redwood's internal backup copies, legal hold requests will pause deletion windows—those details are in the addendum.
[09:05] Luis Ortega: Also adding that for the POC we can set default push interval to 1 minute so your SIEM pulls more timely samples.
[09:12] Daniel Park: That helps.
[09:15] [09:45] Maya Chen: Any questions on the log schema?
[09:48] Riya Mehta: One more—do you include model inputs in the logs or only metadata? There are privacy constraints for PII in prompt text.
[09:55] Luis Ortega: We include an abbreviated hash of the prompt for correlation, and content is only included when configured; default for POC is to exclude full prompt text. If you require content for debugging, we can include it but we'd recommend redaction hooks or content filters.
[10:10] Daniel Park: Hash might be enough for now. How does the hash handle salts—are they static? If two entries have same prompt will they produce same hash?
[10:18] Luis Ortega: Hash is salted per-customer and rotates monthly; identical prompts within rotation window will have same hash allowing correlation, but not reversible.
[10:27] Riya Mehta: That's acceptable.
[10:30] [11:00] Maya Chen: Let's review the concrete artifacts we'll send: SOC2 redacted report, audit log JSONL sample (24h), SAML attribute mapping doc, admin API snippet for cache invalidation, and short dedicated vs hosted comparison.
[11:12] Daniel Park: Good list. For the sample logs—please make sure all IDs are redacted by default or hashed.
[11:18] Luis Ortega: Will do. Redaction note: we replace emails with <redacted_email> or hashed email.
[11:24] [11:45] Omar El-Sayed: If Redwood keeps a troubleshooting copy, what's the retention on that? You mentioned 90 days earlier?
[11:51] Maya Chen: Default troubleshooting retention is 90 days, but we can reduce to 14 days for POC agreements. We'll put that in the addendum.
[11:59] Riya Mehta: We'd like 14 days for now.
[12:01] Maya Chen: Noted. Action item.
[12:05] [12:30] Priya Nair: Quick logistics — I'll schedule the sign-off call once Daniel confirms the SIEM run. Also I'll attach the shared drive link for the sample logs and SOC2 packet after the call.
[12:40] Daniel Park: Expected SIEM run will be this Friday; I'll confirm.
[12:45] Riya Mehta: Also can you include the certificate chain for SAML metadata? We need fingerprint to pre-load into Okta.
[12:51] Luis Ortega: Yes, cert chain and fingerprint will be in the SAML doc.
[12:55] [13:20] Maya Chen: Alright let's recap the next steps — I'll list them in the calendar notes but high level: send SOC2 pack, upload log sample to shared drive, Luis to share admin API snippet and transform mapping, Aerolith to validate in SIEM, and set retention to 14 days for Redwood debug copies during POC.
[13:40] Daniel Park: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[13:44] Riya Mehta: Thanks.
[13:46] Luis Ortega: Thanks everyone, will follow up with links.
[13:50] Priya Nair: Bye.
---
End of transcript.
notes_and_links: Audit log sample: aerolith_audit_20250729.jsonl (uploaded to drive)
